overview: ASMPT Limited (formerly ASM Pacific Technology), headquartered in Singapore and listed on HKEX, is a leading global supplier of back-end semiconductor assembly/packaging equipment and SMT (surface-mount technology) placement equipment used to manufacture semiconductors and electronic devices. The Group reports two segments, Semiconductor Solutions (SEMI, including advanced packaging tools such as thermo-compression bonding/TCB, hybrid bonding, flip-chip, photonics and wire/die bonding) and SMT Solutions (PCB/board assembly placement systems), and operates globally with manufacturing and R&D in Asia (Singapore, China), Europe (Munich) and the Americas and roughly 42% of FY2025/1H2026 revenue sourced from China.

business_model.summary: ASMPT sells capital equipment (wire/die bonders, TCB/hybrid-bonding and other advanced-packaging tools, SMT pick-and-place systems) to semiconductor OSATs, IDMs, foundries and electronics assemblers; revenue is largely transactional/cyclical equipment sales plus a smaller recurring stream from spare parts, consumables and service. Order momentum is tracked via a book-to-bill ratio (1.43x in 1H 2026, highest since 1H 2021) given the project/capex-driven nature of demand.

revenue_streams.name: SEMI Solutions (advanced packaging + mainstream wire/die bonding, photonics)
SMT Solutions (placement equipment for PCB/AI server boards, EV, consumer)

business_model.customer_type: B2B — OSATs, IDMs, foundries, EMS/electronics assemblers; top 5 customers ~19% of 1H2026 revenue (low concentration)
business_model.geographic_mix: China ~42% (1H2026, up from 38% YoY), Asia ex-China ~36%, Europe & Americas ~21%; end-markets: Computing ~33%, Consumer ~18%, Automotive ~12%, Communication ~10%, Industrial ~9% (1H2026)

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest back-end semiconductor assembly/packaging equipment suppliers globally and a top-tier SMT placement equipment vendor; JPMorgan estimates ASMPT's overall TCB (thermo-compression bonding) market share at roughly 30-40%, with a dominant position in logic TCB and share gains emerging in memory (HBM) TCB.

moat_factors.description: Comprehensive chip-to-substrate (C2S) and chip-to-wafer (C2W) TCB portfolio with repeat bulk orders (50+ tool order in July 2026) from OSAT partners of the leading advanced logic customer; over 1,800 patents filed across SEMI and SMT.

Equipment qualification cycles with leading logic and memory customers are lengthy; once qualified into a customer's process flow, tools tend to be repeat-ordered (evidenced by bulk follow-on orders), though hybrid bonding share is still being contested against Besi.
Offers TCB, hybrid bonding, photonics, flip-chip and mass reflow under one roof, positioning it as a one-stop vendor for complex heterogeneous integration/CPO (co-packaged optics) builds.
R&D spend of ~HK$1.0bn in 1H2026 (~12% of revenue) across global centres (Singapore for SEMI, Munich for SMT) sustains a technology lead but is a continuing cost burden in cyclical downturns.

weaknesses: Hybrid bonding (next-gen advanced packaging) leadership currently held by Besi; ASMPT is still in sampling/qualification stage with its second-generation platform
SMT segment faces intense competition from Japanese (Fuji, Yamaha, Panasonic) and other Asian suppliers on price and is more commoditized than advanced packaging
High revenue cyclicality tied to semiconductor capex cycles and a small number of large AI/logic/memory customers' capacity decisions
Divested NEXX (US dispensing/electroplating-related unit) in June 2026 for only ~US$116-120m net proceeds after a weak 2025 performance, highlighting execution risk in non-core M&A/divestment

growth_drivers: AI-driven demand for advanced packaging: TCB, hybrid bonding, photonics and flip-chip tools benefiting from AI accelerator/GPU and HBM memory packaging buildouts; TCB TAM expected to exceed US$1.6bn by 2028
Photonics/co-packaged optics (CPO): Pluggable Optical Transceiver revenue almost tripled YoY to ~US$75m in 1H2026 on 800G+ transceiver demand; CPO engagement with multiple leading global players

SMT recovery driven by AI server board assembly (high-flex, high-force large-format placement) plus China EV demand, alongside gradual recovery in traditional consumer/industrial/automotive end markets
Memory TCB share gains tied to HBM4 rollout timing and an exclusive joint evaluation programme with a key memory player
Panel-level packaging and chip-on-panel tooling as an emerging growth vector leveraging existing TCB technology
Portfolio simplification via NEXX divestiture (June 2026) to focus capital/management attention on core SEMI/SMT advanced packaging growth areas

business.description: Equipment orders are tied to customers' capacity expansion decisions; prior cycles (FY2023 revenue decline) show deep troughs when AI/memory capex pauses.

A large share of AP/TCB revenue is linked to repeat orders from a small number of leading advanced logic and memory (HBM) customers and their OSAT partners; delays in customers' product rollout schedules (e.g., HBM4 timing) directly affect order timing.

business.risk: Technology leadership risk in hybrid bonding
business.description: ASMPT's HB platform is still in sampling/qualification while competitor Besi has an established lead; failure to win qualification could cede the next packaging wave.
SMT is a more mature, competitive market with multiple well-capitalized Japanese and Asian rivals, limiting pricing power outside AI-specific large-format tools.

financial.description: Revenue/costs denominated across USD, EUR, RMB and HKD; reporting currency is HKD (pegged to USD) but input costs and sales mix create translation and transaction exposure, with management citing unfavourable FX as an OPEX headwind in 1H2026.
Unsecured bank borrowings (~HK$2.25bn at 1H2026) are mainly variable-rate syndicated loans; D/E ratio is low (0.130) and partially hedged via interest rate swaps on HK$0.75bn notional.
NEXX disposal closed June 2026 at a price reduced due to weak 2025 performance of the unit; further portfolio actions could carry similar execution/valuation risk.

regulatory.risk: US/allied export controls on semiconductor equipment to China
regulatory.description: Broader toolmaker industry faces expanding US-led export restrictions (covering equipment, components, and maintenance) aimed at China; ASMPT derives ~42% of revenue from China, making it sensitive to any extension of controls to back-end packaging/SMT equipment, even though back-end assembly tools have so far been less targeted than front-end lithography/deposition equipment.

China has added companies (including some Japanese toolmakers) to its own export-control and unreliable-entity lists amid the broader trade dispute; escalation could affect ASMPT's China operations or supply chain.

macro.description: Current order strength is heavily concentrated in AI-related data center, HBM memory and AI server demand; a slowdown in hyperscaler/AI capex would disproportionately hit AP/TCB/photonics bookings that are driving the current growth narrative.
Traditional end markets (consumer electronics, industrial, non-China automotive) remain only in gradual recovery and are sensitive to global growth and interest-rate-driven demand for durable goods.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Back-end semiconductor packaging equipment demand is in a strong AI-driven upcycle (advanced packaging TAM expanding, TCB market alone projected past US$1.6bn by 2028); SMT equipment is recovering alongside AI server board build-outs and a gradual recovery in consumer/industrial/auto demand.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — equipment orders are capex-cycle driven; book-to-bill ratio (1.43x in 1H2026) is the key forward indicator and has swung sharply across past cycles (e.g., FY2023 trough).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect — customers' capex decisions and own variable-rate debt (partially swapped to fixed) are both rate-sensitive; direct balance-sheet leverage is low (D/E 0.130, net cash position).
key_input_costs: Raw materials/components subject to longer lead times noted in 1H2026 outlook

recent_developments.event: Stock trading with a wide analyst target range (HK$84-225) reflecting disagreement on how much of the AI-driven re-rating is sustainable; JPMorgan Overweight with HK$225 target (July 2026) citing 30-40% TCB share and memory TCB share gains; Bank of America upgraded to Buy with HK$150 target in February 2026.
Bassel Haddad appointed Executive Director, positioned as incoming CEO successor as Robin Ng plans to retire — a leadership transition during the current AI upcycle.

1H2026/Q2 2026 results: revenue HK$8.90bn (+42.5% YoY continuing ops), bookings HK$12.75bn (+85.1% YoY), book-to-bill 1.43x (highest since 1H2021), adjusted net profit HK$972.7m (+230.5% YoY); interim dividend raised sharply to HK$0.97/share (2025: HK$0.26).
Received bulk orders for 50+ chip-to-substrate (C2S) TCB tools from OSAT customers of the leading advanced logic customer, reinforcing TCB leadership narrative.
Completed sale of ASMPT NEXX, Inc. to Applied Materials for ~US$120m gross (~US$116m net), following its FY2025 classification as a discontinued operation; NEXX deconsolidated from 3 June 2026.
Announced definitive agreement to sell NEXX to Applied Materials.
Q1 2026 results showed continued sequential acceleration in bookings/revenue, setting up the stronger Q2/1H print; Q1 2026 revenue guidance had been US$470-530m.

FY2025 results: continuing-ops revenue HK$13.74bn (+10.0% YoY), net profit HK$1.085bn (+272.7% YoY) aided by a HK$1.11bn gain on disposal of a joint venture; NEXX first flagged as held-for-divestment/discontinued operation.

items.notes: Midpoint implies +4.8% QoQ and +46.3% YoY; guidance given as above market consensus despite longer lead times for certain materials.
Mainly driven by TCB and Photonics order momentum.

items.target: Growth across both SEMI and SMT segments in 2026
items.notes: Management reiterated confidence despite longer lead times and customers' dynamic AI product rollout schedules (e.g., HBM4 timing).

items.target: Capital additions fully funded by operating cash flow
items.notes: No explicit forward capex range disclosed; management emphasizes self-funded capex and a robust balance sheet (net cash HK$3.63bn at 1H2026).

guidance.management_commentary: Management stated the Group 'remains confident of revenue growth across both SEMI and SMT in 2026' driven by AI infrastructure buildouts and gradual recovery in traditional end markets (consumer, industrial, automotive EVs), while flagging longer lead times for certain materials and the uncertain timing of customers' AI product rollout schedules (particularly HBM4) as watch items. The Board sharply increased the interim dividend to HK$0.97/share (from HK$0.26 in 1H2025), signaling confidence in the earnings recovery.

bull_case: Structural AI-driven demand for advanced packaging (TCB, hybrid bonding, photonics/CPO) positions ASMPT as a key enabler of AI infrastructure buildouts, with a leading ~30-40% TCB market share and record book-to-bill (1.43x, highest since 1H2021)

Operating leverage is flowing through strongly: 1H2026 adjusted operating profit up 220.9% HoH and adjusted net profit up 263.8% HoH on margin expansion plus volume, showing significant earnings torque to the AI upcycle
SMT segment is riding a parallel AI server board assembly boom plus a China EV recovery, diversifying growth drivers beyond pure advanced packaging

Balance sheet is strong (net cash ~HK$3.63bn, D/E 0.130) with capex self-funded from operating cash flow, giving flexibility to keep investing in R&D/capacity through the cycle; interim dividend nearly quadrupled YoY
Portfolio simplification (NEXX divestiture) sharpens management focus on core SEMI/SMT advanced-packaging growth areas
bear_case: Current re-rating is heavily reliant on continued AI/HBM capex strength; any pause or digestion period in hyperscaler/memory capex (as seen in prior cycles, e.g., FY2023 trough) could sharply reverse bookings momentum
Hybrid bonding, the next major advanced-packaging wave, is still led by competitor Besi; ASMPT's second-generation platform remains in customer sampling/qualification with no confirmed wins yet

Elevated China revenue exposure (~42% of 1H2026 revenue) leaves the stock vulnerable to any extension of US/allied semiconductor equipment export controls to back-end packaging or SMT tools, or to Chinese counter-measures
Wide dispersion in analyst price targets (roughly HK$84-225) reflects genuine uncertainty about how much of the current growth rate is sustainable versus cyclical/order-timing-driven
Leadership transition (CEO Robin Ng's planned retirement, successor Bassel Haddad appointed August 2026) introduces execution risk at a critical point in the AI packaging cycle
